name: MoMA PS1
funding: $18M annual operating budget. Subsidiary of The Museum of Modern Art; supported by NYC Department of Cultural Affairs, MoMA Board, and foundation grants.
watch: Leon Black still a trustee after Epstein payments; Fink, Crown and Dubin named in Strike MoMA and the 2024 sit-in.

name: The Metropolitan Museum of Art (The Met)
funding: $330M+ annual budget; $4.4B endowment. City of New York municipal support, admissions, Bloomberg Philanthropies, Tiffany & Co., Bank of America, Leonard A. Lauder bequests.
watch: Koch Plaza name kept since 2014; Sackler name removed only in 2021.
why_flagged: Koch Plaza name kept since 2014; Sackler name removed only in 2021.
records_note: It posts annual reports and audited statements from 2020 to 2025, Form 990s back to 2012, named donor lists and a trustee page.
other_findings: WikiLeaks, 2005-06: Embassy Kuwait notes that Shaykh Nasser Al-Sabah, of the ruling family and owner of a major Islamic art collection, is an honorary board member of the Met. (Cablegate 05KUWAIT2712) | Epstein link · Jeffrey Epstein · documented: The DOJ files released in January 2026 contain a copy of a $5,000 check dated 29 April 2014 from Enhanced Education, a foundation Epstein set up, made out to the Met for the Costume Institute Benefit (the Met Gala). Earlier, press releases from the Jeffrey Epstein VI Foundation listed the Met as receiving gifts from 2010 to 2012. In July 2019 the Met told NBC News it had received no major donations from Epstein or his foundation, and that its only record was his purchase of tickets to two benefits in the early 1990s. The Met did not respond to ARTnews about the 2014 check, and ARTnews does not report whether the check was deposited.

name: Whitney Museum of American Art
funding: $105M annual operating budget. Admissions, board patron giving, Hyundai Motor, Tiffany & Co., Genesis philanthropic initiatives.
watch: Kanders resigned 2019 after protests; Crown family trustee targeted 2025.
why_flagged: Kanders resigned 2019 after protests; Crown family trustee targeted 2025.
records_note: It posts audited statements and Form 990s for 2014 to 2025, names its donors and lists 34 trustees as of October 2026.
other_findings: Epstein link · David A. Ross · documented: David A. Ross directed the Whitney from 1991 to 1998. He told ARTnews he met Epstein in the mid-1990s and that befriending potential museum supporters was "part of my job". Emails in the DOJ files run from 2009 to at least 2016, one says he was "still proud to call you a friend", and Ross says he contacted Epstein in 2019 to show support. Ross resigned from the School of Visual Arts, effective 3 February 2026.

name: Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum
funding: $72M annual operating budget. Admissions, Solomon R. Guggenheim Foundation endowment, Lavazza, BMW Group cultural partnerships.
watch: Refused Sackler gifts 2019, removed the name 2022.
why_flagged: Refused Sackler gifts 2019, removed the name 2022.
records_note: It posts audited statements (2010, 2020, 2021) and Form 990s for 2017 to 2020 on its site; the Form 990s list the trustees.
other_findings: WikiLeaks, 2008-08 to 2010-01: Guggenheim Abu Dhabi is a TDIC project, and the UAE "roundly rejected" Human Rights Watch's labour-abuse findings on Saadiyat. A Baku cable ties the Azerbaijani First Lady's family to plans for a Guggenheim branch. (Cablegate, 3 cables)

name: Centre Pompidou
funding: €130M annual operating budget. French Ministry of Culture subventions (over 65%), admissions, Friends of Centre Pompidou.
watch: €50M Saudi state pledge for the renovation.
why_flagged: €50M Saudi state pledge for the renovation.
records_note: Pompidou posts activity reports from 1973 to 2025 with a finance summary and a named 2025 patron list, but no accounts and no named board.

name: Serpentine Galleries
funding: £9.8M annual budget. Arts Council England National Portfolio Organization (NPO), Bloomberg Philanthropies public pavilion commissions, individual patron circle. Always free admission.
records_note: It files group accounts at Companies House for 2020 to 2025 and lists 14 trustees, but posts no annual reports and no named supporters.

name: Fundació Joan Miró
funding: Private foundation; Generalitat, Barcelona council and Culture Ministry sit on its board. Strategic allies: Fundación BBVA, Fundació la Caixa, Puig. Also Fundació Banc Sabadell, Abertis, Sorigué, Damm.
watch: la Caixa's holding Criteria is the largest shareholder of gas utility Naturgy, which paid 23% of Criteria's 2025 dividends.
why_flagged: la Caixa's holding Criteria is the largest shareholder of gas utility Naturgy, which paid 23% of Criteria's 2025 dividends.
records_note: It posts annual reports for 2023 and 2024 and audited accounts, naming funders and trustees inside the 2024 report.

name: Dia Chelsea
funding: Dia Art Foundation endowment ($110M), board contributions, and New York State Council on the Arts. Always free admission.
watch: Dropped the Sackler name 2019; Schlumberger origin.

name: Barbican Art Gallery & The Curve
funding: £55M operating budget. Funded directly by the City of London Corporation as founder and principal funder, alongside Arts Council England and ticket revenues.
watch: Public civic corporation governance. The Curve gallery remains permanently free to the public, hosting major uncompromised site-specific commissions.

name: The Photographers' Gallery
funding: £4.3M income (FY2025). Arts Council England £919k, Westminster City Council, Deutsche Börse Photography Foundation to 2027, Leica, Polaroid, MPB, Speroni Foundation, John Lyon's Charity, Kusuma Trust.
watch: Kusuma Trust, funded by PartyGaming co-founder Anurag Dikshit's fortune, supports its education programmes. Deutsche Börse is an exchange operator, not Deutsche Bank.
why_flagged: £4.3M income (FY2025). Arts Council England £919k, Westminster City Council, Deutsche Börse Photography Foundation to 2027, Leica, Polaroid, MPB, Speroni Foundation, John Lyon's Charity, Kusuma Trust.
records_note: Names trustees with appointment years and shows corporate partner logos with no date; no annual reports posted, accounts for 2021 to 2025 on the register.

name: Instituto Inhotim
funding: R$ 60M budget. Federal Culture Incentive Law (Lei Rouanet), Vale Cultural Institute civic environmental agreements, and ticket revenues.
watch: Vale, whose 2019 dam collapse killed 270 nearby, pays the operating budget.
why_flagged: Vale, whose 2019 dam collapse killed 270 nearby, pays the operating budget.
records_note: Inhotim posts institutional reports from 2012 to 2025, audited financial statements for most years, sponsor logos by tier with no date, and its full council.

name: MUDAM (Musée d'Art Moderne Grand-Duc Jean)
funding: State-funded national museum; patrons include Clearstream (Deutsche Börse, 2024) and Degroof Petercam (since 2021).
watch: UNVERIFIED: Two patrons verified, full roster not reached.

records_note: Mudam posts activity reports for 2007 to 2025, names its patrons undated, and lists its board, but shows no financial statements.
